title: GERUND & INFINITIVE
notes:
✓ Gerund → the -ing form of a verb used as a noun.

✓ Infinitive → to + base form of a verb.

✓ Swimming is good exercise. → gerund
✓ I want to swim. → infinitive

✓ Both can function as nouns, but their use depends on the verb, expression, or grammatical structure.

title: GERUND
notes:
✓ Gerund → verb + -ing functioning as a noun.

✓ Reading improves your vocabulary.
✓ I enjoy reading.
✓ She is interested in learning English.

◆ A GERUND CAN FUNCTION AS
✓ Subject → Swimming is fun.
✓ Object → I enjoy swimming.
✓ Object of a preposition → She is good at swimming.
✓ Subject complement → Her favorite activity is reading.

title: GERUND AS SUBJECT
notes:
✓ A gerund can be the subject of a sentence.

✓ Reading is important.
✓ Learning English takes time.
✓ Exercising regularly improves your health.

✓ When a gerund phrase is the subject, it normally takes a singular verb.

✓ Swimming is good exercise.
✓ Studying hard helps students succeed.

⚠️ Treat the gerund phrase as one activity.

title: VERBS FOLLOWED BY GERUNDS
notes:
✓ Many common verbs are followed by a gerund.

✓ enjoy → I enjoy reading.
✓ avoid → She avoids driving at night.
✓ finish → He finished studying.
✓ mind → Do you mind waiting?
✓ suggest → She suggested going home.
✓ consider → They considered moving.
✓ keep → Keep working.
✓ practice → He practices speaking English.
✓ miss → I miss seeing my friends.
✓ admit → He admitted making a mistake.
✓ deny → She denied taking the money.
✓ risk → Don't risk losing your job.

✓ These verbs are commonly tested in grammar questions.

title: VERB + GERUND EXPRESSIONS
notes:
✓ Common expressions followed by gerunds:

✓ can't stand → I can't stand waiting.
✓ can't help → I can't help laughing.
✓ feel like → I feel like sleeping.
✓ give up → He gave up smoking.
✓ look forward to → I look forward to meeting you.
✓ be worth → It is worth seeing.
✓ have difficulty → She has difficulty understanding.
✓ spend time → He spends time reading.

⚠️ In 'look forward to', to is a preposition, so use a gerund.

❌ I look forward to meet you.
✓ I look forward to meeting you.

title: GERUND AFTER PREPOSITIONS
notes:
✓ A verb following a preposition normally takes the -ing form.

✓ She is good at drawing.
✓ He left without saying goodbye.
✓ They talked about moving abroad.
✓ Before leaving, turn off the lights.
✓ Thank you for helping me.

◆ PATTERN
preposition + V-ing.

✓ Common prepositions → at, in, on, for, about, without, before, after, by.

title: INFINITIVE
notes:
✓ Infinitive → to + base form of a verb.

✓ to study
✓ to work
✓ to learn
✓ to travel

◆ INFINITIVES CAN EXPRESS
✓ Purpose → I went there to study.
✓ Intention → She plans to travel.
✓ Desire → He wants to learn.
✓ Decision → They decided to leave.

title: VERBS FOLLOWED BY INFINITIVES
notes:
✓ Common verbs followed by to + infinitive:

✓ want → I want to learn.
✓ need → She needs to study.
✓ decide → He decided to leave.
✓ hope → We hope to win.
✓ plan → They plan to travel.
✓ promise → She promised to help.
✓ agree → He agreed to come.
✓ refuse → They refused to pay.
✓ expect → I expect to finish soon.
✓ offer → She offered to help.
✓ learn → He learned to drive.
✓ manage → She managed to escape.
✓ afford → I can't afford to buy it.

◆ PATTERN
verb + to + base verb.

title: PURPOSE INFINITIVE
notes:
✓ To + infinitive can explain the purpose of an action.

✓ I went to the library to study.
✓ She saved money to buy a laptop.
✓ He called me to ask a question.

✓ Meaning → 'in order to'.

✓ He went to the shop to buy food.
= He went to the shop in order to buy food.

⚠️ Use the base verb after to.

❌ I went there to studying.
✓ I went there to study.

title: VERB + OBJECT + INFINITIVE
notes:
✓ Some verbs are followed by an object + to-infinitive.

✓ want → I want you to come.
✓ ask → She asked me to help.
✓ tell → He told me to wait.
✓ advise → They advised us to leave.
✓ encourage → She encouraged him to study.
✓ remind → He reminded me to call.
✓ invite → They invited us to join.
✓ allow → The teacher allowed us to leave.

◆ PATTERN
verb + object + to + base verb.

title: BARE INFINITIVE
notes:
✓ Bare infinitive → base verb without 'to'.

◆ COMMON AFTER MODAL VERBS
✓ can → She can swim.
✓ must → You must study.
✓ should → He should leave.
✓ will → They will come.

✓ Also used after make and let:
✓ The teacher made him apologize.
✓ His parents let him go.

⚠️ Do not add 'to' after a modal.

❌ She can to swim.
✓ She can swim.

title: GERUND OR INFINITIVE: BOTH POSSIBLE
notes:
✓ Some verbs can be followed by either a gerund or an infinitive with little or no change in meaning.

✓ like → I like reading.
✓ like → I like to read.

✓ love → She loves swimming.
✓ love → She loves to swim.

✓ hate → He hates waiting.
✓ hate → He hates to wait.

✓ prefer → I prefer walking.
✓ prefer → I prefer to walk.

✓ The choice can sometimes depend on context, style, or emphasis.

title: VERBS WHERE MEANING CHANGES
notes:
✓ Some verbs change meaning depending on whether they are followed by a gerund or infinitive.

◆ STOP + GERUND → stop an activity.
✓ I stopped smoking. → I quit smoking.

◆ STOP + INFINITIVE → stop one action in order to do another.
✓ I stopped to smoke. → I stopped another activity in order to smoke.

◆ REMEMBER + GERUND → remember a past action.
✓ I remember meeting him.

◆ REMEMBER + INFINITIVE → remember a duty/action that must be done.
✓ Remember to call me.

◆ FORGET + GERUND → forget a past experience.
✓ I'll never forget meeting her.

◆ FORGET + INFINITIVE → fail to remember to do something.
✓ I forgot to call him.

title: TRY + GERUND / INFINITIVE
notes:
✓ Try + gerund → experiment with a method to see if it works.

✓ Try restarting the computer.

✓ Try + infinitive → make an effort to do something difficult.

✓ Try to restart the computer.

✓ Compare:
✓ Try opening the window. → Experiment with this solution.
✓ Try to open the window. → Make an effort to open it.

title: REGRET + GERUND / INFINITIVE
notes:
✓ Regret + gerund → feel sorry about something that happened in the past.

✓ I regret telling him the secret.

✓ Regret + infinitive → formal expression used to announce bad news.

✓ We regret to inform you that your application was unsuccessful.

✓ Meaning changes according to the form.

title: MEAN + GERUND / INFINITIVE
notes:
✓ Mean + gerund → involve or result in something.

✓ This job means working late.

✓ Mean + infinitive → intend to do something.

✓ I meant to call you yesterday.

✓ Compare:
✓ This job means working late. → involves.
✓ I meant to call you. → intended.

title: GO ON + GERUND / INFINITIVE
notes:
✓ Go on + gerund → continue the same activity.

✓ She went on talking.
→ She continued talking.

✓ Go on + infinitive → finish one action and then begin another.

✓ She went on to explain the next point.
→ She then began explaining something new.

title: GERUND & INFINITIVE AFTER ADJECTIVES
notes:
✓ Adjective + infinitive is common when describing feelings, reactions, or difficulty.

✓ I am happy to help.
✓ She is ready to leave.
✓ It is difficult to understand.
✓ He was surprised to see her.

✓ Certain adjective expressions use preposition + gerund.

✓ He is good at swimming.
✓ She is interested in learning.
✓ They are afraid of failing.

✓ Remember the preposition rule → preposition + V-ing.

title: GERUND VS INFINITIVE
notes:
◆ GERUND → V-ing used as a noun.
✓ I enjoy reading.

◆ INFINITIVE → to + base verb.
✓ I want to read.

✓ After a preposition → GERUND.
✓ She is interested in learning.

✓ After many modal verbs → BARE INFINITIVE.
✓ She can learn.

✓ After verbs such as enjoy, avoid, finish → GERUND.
✓ He enjoys reading.

✓ After verbs such as want, decide, hope → INFINITIVE.
✓ He wants to read.

title: COMMON ERRORS
notes:
❌ I enjoy to read.
✓ I enjoy reading.

❌ She wants going home.
✓ She wants to go home.

❌ He is good at to play football.
✓ He is good at playing football.

❌ I look forward to meet you.
✓ I look forward to meeting you.

❌ She suggested to go home.
✓ She suggested going home.

❌ He made me to apologize.
✓ He made me apologize.

❌ She can to swim.
✓ She can swim.

❌ I stopped to smoke. → incorrect if the intended meaning is 'I quit smoking.'
✓ I stopped smoking.

title: EXAM GUIDE
notes:
◆ 1. After a preposition → GERUND.
✓ interested in learning.

◆ 2. After enjoy, avoid, finish, suggest, consider → GERUND.

◆ 3. After want, need, decide, hope, plan, promise → TO-INFINITIVE.

◆ 4. After a modal verb → BARE INFINITIVE.
✓ can go, must study, should leave.

◆ 5. Verb + object + to-infinitive → want me to go, tell him to wait.

◆ 6. Purpose → TO-INFINITIVE.
✓ I went there to study.

◆ 7. Stop/remember/forget/try/regret/mean/go on → check the meaning before choosing gerund or infinitive.

◆ 8. Keep grammatical forms parallel when joining actions.
✓ She likes reading and writing.

✓ Golden rule → Learn which verbs take gerunds, which take infinitives, and which allow both with a change in meaning.
